# Wisdom of Solomon Chapter 4 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Wisdom 4 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/WIS_004_page_001.jpg

---

4:1 Better is childlessness with virtue, for immortality is in the memory of virtue; because it is recognized both by God and by men.

4:2 When it is present they imitate it, and they long for it when it has departed; and throughout all time it marches crowned in triumph, victorious in the contest for prizes that are undefiled.

4:3 But the prolific brood of the ungodly will be of no use, and none of their illegitimate shoots will strike deep root or take firm hold.

4:4 For even if they put out branches in season, they will be shaken by the wind, having no root, and by the force of the winds they will be uprooted.

4:5 Their branches will be broken off before they come to maturity, and their fruit will be useless, unripe for eating, fit for nothing.

4:6 For children born of unlawful unions are witnesses against their parents when they are examined.

4:7 But the righteous, even if he dies early, will be at rest.

4:8 For old age is not honored for length of time, nor measured by number of years;

4:9 but understanding is grey hair for men, and a blameless life is ripe old age.

4:10 There was one who pleased God and was loved by him, and while living among sinners he was taken up.

4:11 He was caught up lest wickedness alter his understanding, or deceit beguile his soul.

4:12 For the fascination of wickedness obscures good things, and the roving of desire undermines the simple mind.

4:13 Having been made perfect in a short time, he fulfilled long years;

4:14 for his soul was pleasing to the Lord, therefore he took him quickly from the midst of wickedness.

4:15 Yet the peoples see and do not understand, neither do they take such a thing to heart: that grace and mercy are with his elect, and care for his holy ones.

4:16 And the righteous man who has died will condemn the ungodly who are living, and youth completed early will condemn the prolonged old age of the unrighteous.

4:17 For they will see the end of the wise man, and will not understand what the Lord planned for him, and why he kept him safe.

4:18 They will see, and they will hold him in contempt; but the Lord will laugh at them.

4:19 And after this they will become a dishonored corpse and an outrage among the dead forever; because he will shatter them speechless and headlong, and he will shake them from their foundations, and they will be left utterly desolate; they will be in anguish, and their memory will perish.

4:20 They will come with dread to the reckoning of their sins, and their lawless deeds will convict them to their face.

---

*EMET notes: 4:10 alludes to Enoch (Gen 5:24 — "he pleased God and was not, for God took him"). "Taken up" (metetethe) is the LXX term for Enoch. Verse 12's "fascination of wickedness" renders goēteia — literally sorcery/enchantment; wickedness is figured as a magical lure. Verse 13: "made perfect in a short time" — teleiōtheis, the word used for the completion/perfection of a sacrifice — rich theological vocabulary.*
